failures.evidence: CI run 41393622961 at b59a0203, job 125113156314: `--- FAIL: TestPodUpdateTellsItsWorkerNothingHoweverTheRoundEnds/the_pod_went_without_its_round (60.19s)` with `podupdate_test.go:1188: timed out waiting for implementer: its round to end`. I reproduced it on my own PostgreSQL (127.0.0.1:5457, started for this role alone so no sibling shares it): `go test ./internal/daemon -run 'TestPodUpdateTellsItsWorkerNothingHoweverTheRoundEnds' -count=20` fails 3 of 60 subtest runs, and a second such run failed 4 more times, every one of them `the_pod_went_without_its_round` at :1188 except one `the_drift_cleared_over_the_pod_that_replaced_the_round's_own`. Both failing cases are the ones whose `end` closure is `rig.tickBackIn(podUpdateReplacementPod)` -- a single sweep -- followed by `rig.awaitClaim(implementer, "its round to end", UpdateRound == "")`. awaitClaim polls the claim through testwait.Eventually and never sweeps, so when that one sweep does not end the round -- the machines have not yet recorded the departure the rewritten snapshot already shows, so the live read still holds the old pod -- nothing drives another sweep and the wait runs out. This is the same class as round 16's nine single-tick assertions, and the exact hazard I recorded in my round-16 handoff and PR line: that this test is gated by a non-sweeping awaitClaim and was robust only because its worker was quiesced. Round 18's record and gone-first rules changed what that one sweep decides, and the hazard became a failure. The product is not at fault: a real daemon sweeps every 250 ms, so the round ends on the next tick. Fix: make that wait sweep while it waits, as awaitReplacement already does for the replacement assertions -- a bounded sweep-and-check of `UpdateRound == ""` -- for the two cases whose end is tickBackIn. Do not weaken the assertion itself: it must still require the round to have ended and the worker to have been sent nothing.

Structurally there are exactly two writers: leftPodRoundAt sets it, clearUpdate clears it, and clearUpdate has four callers -- openPodUpdate replacing a round, the plugin-relaunch leave, leaveRound, and retire. letGo, which a suspension uses and which clears the locator, does not clear it. retire does, with its reason documented (a retired claim runs nothing on the round's pod, so a round left on it would be read against whatever pod the replacement makes); that is the one clearer besides the round's end and I record it as an observation rather than a defect. By driving: the relaunch and store-durability cases are TestPodUpdateRecordsTheRoundAClaimLeavesAndWhetherItHadAnswered (which asserts the stored copy), the suspension and letGo case is TestPodUpdateASuspensionKeepsAClaimOutOfTheRoundItLeft (which asserts Locator == nil and the column intact and the late answer refused naming the round), and I drove the restart myself in a throwaway: after h.restart() the column still reads the round left, and the late answer is still refused.
